title: Detection pre-label QA: two models vs ground truth
scenario: Two detection models' normalised centre-format predictions are converted to pixels and greedily matched (IoU >= 0.5, same label) against reviewer ground truth. Each model is scored independently, and Test 2 reports precision/recall/F1, auto-accept images and the best model.

verified.why_correct: The halving and the width/height scaling look easy to get backwards, but this is exactly the README formula for continuous pixel edges. No +1 is needed because edges are not inclusive pixel indices.
The key (iou, -index) looks odd, but max() then takes the highest IoU and, among equal IoUs, the smallest index, which is the earliest ground-truth box as rule 2 requires.

bugs.title: Area computed with inclusive +1
bugs.old: return max(0.0, box.x2 - box.x1) * max(0.0, box.y2 - box.y1)
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_yolo_images: yolo-s img-03 and img-04 become {tp 0, fp 1, fn 1}. Test 2: yolo totals are (8, 2, 4, 0.8, 0.667, 0.727) instead of (10, 0, 2, 1.0, 0.833, 0.909), img-03/img-04 drop out of yolo's auto_accept, and best_model flips to 'detr-v2'. detr-v2 is unaffected.
bugs.why: The +1 belongs to inclusive integer pixel indices, but these boxes use continuous edges. Each area is inflated while the intersection is not, so every IoU shrinks and borderline matches (yolo-s img-03 at exactly 0.5, img-04 at 0.51) fall below the threshold.
bugs.unblocks: yolo-s rows in Test 1 and yolo totals/auto_accept in Test 2; it also exposes B3.
hints: yolo-s loses two matches whose boxes overlap the ground truth by about half. Compute their IoU by hand from the README.
Compare area() with the README's geometry section.
Remove the + 1 from both factors in area().
probes: Why did the large boxes still match while the small ones flipped?
Why does a +1 in area but not in the intersection always lower IoU?

bugs.title: Shallow copy of the ground-truth pool
bugs.old: unmatched = {image: list(boxes) for image, boxes in ground_truth.items()}
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_yolo_images: yolo-s shows FPs (fn 0) on every image detr-v2 matched (img-01, 02, 04, 06, 07, 08, and the truck on img-05). Test 2: yolo totals are (3, 7, 0, 0.3, 1.0, 0.462), auto_accept is `{'detr-v2': [], 'yolo-s': []}`, and best_model is 'detr-v2'. detr-v2's own counts stay correct.
bugs.why: dict() copies only the outer mapping. The per-image lists are still the loader's lists, so pool.pop() removes detr-v2's matches from the shared ground truth. yolo-s is then scored against what detr-v2 left over, and auto_accept (which checks gt[image]) sees emptied lists.
bugs.unblocks: Most of yolo-s in Test 1, both models' auto_accept, and best_model.
hints: yolo-s gets FPs on images where its boxes are perfect, but only on images detr-v2 already matched. What do the two models share?
Look at the 'copy' evaluate_model makes before matching, and at what match_image does to the pool.
dict(ground_truth) is shallow. Copy each list: {image: list(boxes) for image, boxes in ground_truth.items()}.
probes: Why did detr-v2's auto_accept change too, even though detr-v2 is evaluated first?
Would copy.copy(ground_truth) have fixed it? What about copy.deepcopy?

bugs.title: IoU threshold made strict
bugs.symptom: Masked by B1. Once B1 is fixed: Test 1 test_yolo_images shows yolo-s img-03 as {tp 0, fp 1, fn 1}; Test 2 yolo totals are (9, 1, 3, 0.9, 0.75, 0.818) and img-03 is missing from yolo's auto_accept. best_model is still yolo-s.
bugs.why: The spec matches at IoU >= 0.5. yolo-s's img-03 sign box covers exactly half of the ground truth (IoU 0.5) and is rejected by `>`.
bugs.unblocks: yolo-s img-03 in Test 1, plus yolo totals/auto_accept.
hints: After the area fix, one yolo-s image is still a miss. What is its IoU exactly?
Check the threshold comparison in match_image against rule 2.
probes: Why was this invisible while area() added +1?
Why can this data test an exact 0.5 boundary with floats (what is special about 128/512 and 64/512)?

context_qa.q: What does load_predictions return, and which predictions does it keep?
context_qa.a: A nested mapping model -> image_id -> list of (score, Box) in file order. It drops rows whose image is not in images.csv, whose score is missing/blank, or whose score is below MIN_SCORE (0.30), and converts each box to pixels with from_normalized_center.

context_qa.q: What does load_ground_truth return for an image with no reviewer boxes?
context_qa.a: An empty list. The result has one key for every image in images.csv (built with gt.get(image, [])); rows for unknown images such as img-12 are ignored.

context_qa.q: How does match_image use the pool argument?
context_qa.a: It loops over predictions sorted by descending score, collects (iou, index) candidates from `pool` with the same label that pass the threshold check, asks pick_best for one, and pops that index out of `pool`. It returns (tp, fp); the caller reads fn as len(pool) afterwards.

context_qa.q: In what order are models evaluated in build_report?
context_qa.a: sorted(preds), so detr-v2 first, then yolo-s. Both calls to evaluate_model receive the same `gt` dict object from load_ground_truth.
In build_report, after a model's counts are built: sorted images i where gt[i] is non-empty and that model's counts have fp == 0 and fn == 0.

context_qa.q: Which IoUs sit close to the 0.5 threshold in this data?
context_qa.a: yolo-s on img-03 (sign, a 128x64 box inside a 128x128 ground truth) and yolo-s on img-04 (car, roughly a 100x51 box inside a 100x100 ground truth). Every other matched pair is well above 0.8.
